content.comment_body: I developed a program for a client and encountered something unusual. For this project, I created a User Defined Function (UDF) that I needed to use multiple times, each sequence involving timers, logical functions, and several markers within each UDF. However, it appears the software automatically assigns special markers in a way that isn't clear, sometimes resulting in the screen displaying a different color unexpectedly. The workaround involves manually arranging all the special markers first, followed by the UDFs, then completing the program—though this process is inconvenient.

You're correct; the software allocates flags within the UDFs in the sequence they become available, including special flags. The only way to prevent this is through the manual method you've described. Alternatively, you could avoid using flags in the UDF, and there are other options to prevent recursive issues.
The blocks B002, B003, B004, and the open terminal X1 replace the function of a flag.

analysis.insight_summary: Users note that when working with User Defined Functions (UDFs) and using markers and special markers in the software, marker assignment feels automated and not clearly explained, resulting in side effects like unplanned screen color changes. Manually sorting marker assignments can solve the problem but is not efficient and adds frustration. There is a lack of understanding of how marker assignment works within the UDF, and users want greater transparency and control.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect straightforward and transparent assignment of markers and special markers in UDFs, avoiding unpredictable results from automatic allocation. They seek a workflow that minimizes manual work and offers better usability.
